findings.description: Sub-identifier accumulation in OID decoding builds arbitrarily large integers from attacker-controlled multi-byte sub-IDs, giving super-linear CPU/memory cost for large inputs
findings.code_snippet:
while nextSubId >= 128:
    subId = (subId << 7) + (nextSubId & 0x7F)
    if index >= substrateLen:
        raise error.SubstrateUnderrunError(...)
    nextSubId = chunk[index]
    index += 1
oid += ((subId << 7) + nextSubId,)
findings.reasoning: The inner loop (decoder.py ~lines 421-440, flagged by Query 1 at line 421/430 and Query 2 at 421-438) advances index on every iteration and raises SubstrateUnderrunError at end of input, so it terminates and is bounded by the input length. However, subId grows without limit as Python big-int shifts accumulate, so a long run of continuation bytes (0x80-0xFF) produces a very large integer per sub-identifier. Repeated shifts make the cost roughly quadratic in the length of that sub-identifier. Exploitation requires the application to feed attacker-controlled BER data to the decoder and to accept large inputs. No explicit size cap is applied in this code path, so the risk is real but limited by input size and needs a large payload.

evidence.code_context: Inner loop: while nextSubId >= 128: subId = (subId << 7) + (nextSubId & 0x7F); index bounds check; nextSubId = chunk[index]; index += 1. Outer loop: while index < substrateLen.
evidence.dataflow_analysis: chunk comes from the decoded substrate, which is attacker-controlled input. Length is bounded by the input buffer, not by a configured maximum.
evidence.notes: Termination is guaranteed, so this is not an unbounded loop. The concern is super-linear cost from big-int growth on very long sub-IDs. Other flagged loops in valueDecoder/indefLenValueDecoder consume input per iteration and are similar or lower risk.

findings.description: Repeated bytes concatenation (header += component) inside a loop bounded by an attacker-controlled length gives quadratic cost on large constructed encodings
findings.reasoning: The loop (decoder.py ~325-335, flagged by Query 1 at line 330) terminates once the substrate position reaches the declared length, so it is bounded. The declared length comes from the attacker, though. Each iteration does `header += component`, which copies the accumulated bytes, so the total cost is quadratic in the number of components. This is a bounded algorithmic-cost issue, not an unbounded loop, and its impact depends on input size. It is rated low and needs manual review.

evidence.code_context: while substrate.tell() - original_position < length: for component in decodeFun(...): ... ; header += component
evidence.dataflow_analysis: length is taken from the attacker-supplied BER length field. Loop progresses only as substrate.tell() advances, so it terminates at end of input.
evidence.notes: Same class of cost issue as the OID accumulation finding. Most other flagged loops in this file consume input per iteration and are not separate vulnerabilities.

findings.description: Flagged call to getattr in pyasn1 schema object singleton initialization; not attacker-controlled
findings.code_snippet:
op_names = [name
                        for typ in (str, int, list, dict)
                        for name in dir(typ)
                        if (name not in cls.skipMethods and
                            name.startswith('__') and
                            name.endswith('__') and
                            callable(getattr(typ, name)))]
findings.reasoning: The getattr call at line 222 iterates over a hardcoded tuple of built-in types (str, int, list, dict) and their dunder attribute names obtained from dir(). The attribute name and target object are both developer-controlled constants at class-initialization time; no external input reaches getattr. This is a benign introspection pattern used to build a set of blocked operator methods for the ASN.1 schema object, so it is not a code injection vulnerability.

evidence.code_context: def __new__(cls): ... op_names = [name for typ in (str, int, list, dict) for name in dir(typ) if (name not in cls.skipMethods and name.startswith('__') and name.endswith('__') and callable(getattr(typ, name)))]; for name in set(op_names): setattr(cls, name, getPlug(name))
evidence.dataflow_analysis: No user-controlled source; typ comes from a literal tuple and name comes from dir(typ).
evidence.notes: Dangerous-call heuristic triggered only by use of getattr.
